newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL AIM TO USURP CHAMPIONS AT OLD TRAFFORD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL AIM TO USURP CHAMPIONS AT OLD TRAFFORD.

text.p: There is one team above all others that Manchester United want to beat every season -- and it is not neighbours Manchester City.
Likewise everyone connected with Liverpool is consumed with an over-riding desire to also beat one particular team -- and it is not necessarily their neighbours Everton.

No, the two clubs whose rivalry holds no place for friendship, shared romance or sentiment are Manchester United and Liverpool, and when they meet on Saturday at Old Trafford for their 127th league clash the desire for victory for both sets of players and supporters will be even more intense than ever.

Saturday's match -- kicking off at at the unusual hour of 11.15 am (1015 GMT) to cater to the demands of live television -- is their first meeting since Manchester United beat Liverpool 1-0 in the F.A. Cup final in May to clinch their second league and cup double in three seasons.
As if winning on Saturday to avenge that defeat wasn't incentive enough, Liverpool take the field against the champions as league leaders.
A rare win at Old Trafford will confirm them as a side with a realistic chance of winning the league and ending United's recent dominance of the title race.

Since Liverpool last won the league for a record 18th time in 1990, United have been champions three times, won the double twice, the European Cup Winners Cup, the F.A. Cup three times, and the Football League Cup.

In contrast, Liverpool have won the F.A. Cup once and the League Cup once and their domination of the English game in the 1970s and 1980s when United were consistently also-rans is beginning to fade in the memory.
Liverpool fans can almost begrudgingly allow their neighbours Everton the occasional bauble -- but for United to totally outshine them for more than half-a-decade is too much to bear.
The bitter rivalry between them goes back 102 years when both clubs began to emerge as among the most powerful in Lancashire.
Their battles for domination have resulted in highly charged passionate high-scoring affairs down the years -- and not just when major prizes are at stake.
Last week in a reserve match a crunching tackle by Liverpool's Neil Ruddock broke both of Andy Cole's legs and United's record signing is now sidelined for at least three months.

Two seasons ago Ruddock inflamed United's supporters when he folded over Eric Cantona's trademark upturned collar and if the defender plays in place of the injured Dominic Matteo he can be sure of a torrid reception from the Old Trafford fans.
It was in this fixture a year ago that Cantona returned to the United side after his eight-month ban from the game -- and scored with a late penalty to force a 2-2 draw.
And it was another Cantona goal that broke Liverpool hearts and gave United victory in the F.A. Cup Final in May.
While United celebrated their victory and second double, older Liverpool fans were also remembering the day United effectively stopped them winning the treble in 1977.

Liverpool had already won the league and were about to go on to win the European Cup, but United's 2-1 victory in the cup final at Wembley ended their dreams of achieving a feat no English club has yet managed.

Over the last six seasons Liverpool have won four of their 12 league matches, United three while five have been drawn. But Liverpool have not won at Old Trafford since 1990 and have only beaten United twice there in the league in the last 14 seasons.
If they really are serious about inheriting United's title, there would be no better place for Liverpool to win than at Old Trafford on Saturday.
